name: Conor J. Walsh
title: Paul A. Maeder Professor of Engineering and Applied Sciences
department: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences; Materials Science and Mechanical Engineering
fitReason: A direct assistive-robot ML option with personalized sensor fusion and embedded learned control, rather than rehabilitation hardware alone. A CS-focused project could target intention models, robust multimodal inference or human-in-the-loop adaptation; clinical or fabrication expertise may still be important.

physicalEvidence.summary: The August 2, 2025 Nature Communications study deploys a personalized two-layer neural classifier for UP/HOLD/DOWN shoulder intention using IMUs and compression sensors, combined with a physics-based hysteresis model to control an actual pneumatic shoulder robot. TensorFlow Lite inference and control run onboard a BeagleBone at 100 Hz. Nine participants completed in-lab assessment and two demonstrated untethered home use. The paper identifies limitations in fatigue, weighted-object interactions, independent donning and inference of subtle movements; this is not a general robot policy or proven long-term rehabilitation result. Current lab membership lists first author James Arnold and coauthor David Pont, supporting own-group attribution.

shortVisit.summary: The live opportunities page lists graduate admissions, postdoctoral/staff posts and a post-BS/MS Research Fellow role requiring at least 12 months and two years of clinical research experience. Its generic interest in candidates at all levels does not establish an eight-week external-master’s visitor invitation. A Visiting Graduate Students heading on the people page contains no current intake terms.
